title: start_spec drops signal description and title: spec agent receives proposed_resolution only
description:
When start_spec is called with a signal_id, resolve_requirement in start_spec.rs reads the signal record and returns only the proposed_resolution field as the {{input}} requirement. When proposed_resolution is non-empty the signal's title and description are entirely absent from the spec prompt.

This causes three concrete problems:
1. The spec's ## Raw Requirement section reads as an implementation plan rather than a problem statement, because proposed_resolution is the 'how' not the 'what' or 'why'.
2. The spec's ## Description section lacks the richer context held in description — specific state names, acceptance criteria, cross-signal dependencies referenced in prose. For example, signal b0000005 defines the conductor state names (idle, signal_selected, spec_in_progress, ...) only in description; the spec agent authoring from proposed_resolution alone cannot enumerate them.
3. Backlinks to dependent specs may be missing because cross-signal dependencies mentioned in description (e.g. 'after moeb signal a1000046 is resolved') never reach the spec agent.

The drop happens at start_spec.rs lines 160-172 in the read_signal_from_file function.
proposed_resolution:
Modify read_signal_from_file in src/moeb/src/tools/start_spec.rs to compose all three fields when both description and proposed_resolution are present:

  Title: <title>

  Problem: <description>

  Proposed resolution: <proposed_resolution>

When only one of description or proposed_resolution is non-empty, fall through to the existing single-field logic. When both are empty, fall back to the title-only format. Update start_spec_tests.rs to assert that a signal with all three fields populated produces all three sections in the resolved requirement string.
